title: Elena Verna on Product-Led Growth, B2B Growth Loops, Freemyth vs Freemium, and Pricing Strategy
guest_title: Head of Growth at Amplitude, former Growth Advisor at Miro, Dropbox, SurveyMonkey

segments.speaker: Lenny Rachitsky
segments.text: Elena, you are one of the world's foremost experts on Product-Led Growth (PLG). How do you define PLG for companies transitioning from sales-led growth?

segments.speaker: Elena Verna
segments.text: Product-Led Growth isn't just a marketing tactic or self-serve checkout. PLG means your product is the primary driver of customer acquisition, retention, and expansion. In sales-led models, people talk to human sales reps before experiencing value. In PLG, users experience product value first, and monetization follows value realization.

segments.speaker: Elena Verna
segments.text: There are three fundamental growth loops in PLG: 1) Acquisition Loop: How existing user activity naturally invites or attracts new users (e.g., Miro boards shared with external collaborators, Figma links, Typeform signatures). 2) Retention Loop: How product usage creates habit loops and compounding data value (e.g. stored notes in Notion or project boards in Linear). 3) Monetization Loop: How organic individual usage crosses paywall triggers or usage thresholds, converting individual power users into enterprise team contracts.

segments.speaker: Lenny Rachitsky
segments.text: What is the biggest mistake companies make when choosing between Free Trial and Freemium?

segments.speaker: Elena Verna
segments.text: The biggest mistake is offering a 14-day Free Trial for a product with an activation period longer than 14 days! If your product takes 30 days for a team to establish a habit, a 14-day trial kicks users out right before they experience the aha-moment. Freemium works best when you can offer a perpetual free tier with feature gates or usage caps. Free trial works best when the time-to-value is very fast (minutes or hours) and urgency is needed.
